title: MCTL event envelope v1
description: A signal that something happened, never a copy of it. The envelope carries identity and references only; the content stays in its system of record and is hydrated by the consumer through that system's own tools. Closed on purpose: an extra field is how a body would start riding the transport. Serialized envelopes are also capped at 4096 UTF-8 bytes, which JSON Schema cannot express and consumers enforce.

id.description: Globally unique and stable across redelivery: the deduplication key. Producers derive it from the source's own identity (e.g. the Telegram event_id, the X-GitHub-Delivery id), never from a random value generated at publish time.

type.description: Exactly three dotted, lower-case segments: <domain>.<entity>.<action>, e.g. telegram.message.created, github.pull_request.opened.

source.description: The producing service, e.g. mctl-telegram, mctl-api.

occurred_at.description: RFC 3339 with an explicit offset: when the source observed the fact, not when it was published. The pattern bounds every field's range; day-of-month validity (e.g. 02-30) is enforced by consumers, which parse the value.

correlation_id.description: Carried unchanged through producer, stream, channel, Claude and audit so one fact can be traced end to end.

subject.description: References to the thing the event is about. Strings only, each at most 256 characters: a nested object, list or unbounded number is refused because that is where content would hide.
